queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

understanding.life_context: Building something of their own. Feels determined; closest to "I've retired and feel lost" and "I keep comparing myself to others".

hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
hook.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
hook.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
hook.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
hook.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
alternates.setting: Letter from Alameda, California, 18 April 1900, after laying down his role as leader.
alternates.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.translation: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.why: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.
